messages:
maya: Ran a full perf pass on TP all-reduce last night. Seeing big spikes when chunking around 128KB-512KB.

maya: Setup: 8-way TP across 8 GPUs, seq len 1024, kv-cache warm, batching steady at 4 requests.

maya: Profiling notes (nvprof + trace): allreduce time jumps from ~1.1ms to ~8.4ms once msg size > 128KB. CPU side idle — GPU waiting on comm.

maya: log snippet:
```
allreduce(chunk=64KB)  -> 1.2ms
allreduce(chunk=128KB) -> 2.6ms
allreduce(chunk=256KB) -> 6.8ms
allreduce(chunk=512KB) -> 9.1ms
```

omar: interesting, did you try changing NCCL proto/algo? NCCL_PROTO=LL128 helps larger msgs usually.

maya: tried NCCL_ALGO=RING (default) vs NCCL_ALGO=TREE. TREE reduced the 256KB -> 256KB case to ~3.0ms.

justin: can you paste the exact envs you toggled? also whether NVLink or PCIe topology used, that changes tree benefits.

maya: envs I tested:
```
NCCL_ALGO=RING
NCCL_PROTO=LL
NCCL_ALGO=TREE
NCCL_PROTO=LL128
```
Topology: 2x DGX-style NVLink plane (4+4), cross-plane via PCIe.

li: if tree helps, might be because ring does N-1 hops so big messages multiply cost. but tree can add overhead for small msgs.

li: can we instrument per-hop bandwidth? cpu profiler currently only shows aggregate allreduce time.

maya: attached a small perf timeline in trace (pasted):
```
Trace: GPU0 compute 12ms | allreduce 6.8ms | GPU0 idle 3ms
GPU1 compute 11.8ms | allreduce 6.8ms | GPU1 idle 3.2ms
```

infra-bot: @maya deployed a nightly kernel selection test run on 8GPU-cluster (run id: 2026-03-16-0823). Logs: /runs/2026-03-16/176800

maya: another weird thing — when KV cache is sharded across TP boundaries we see larger msgs (prefix cache flush) causing the large allreduce bursts.

omar: that suggests batching heuristics should avoid creating big cross-TP reductions. maybe split KV flush into smaller chunks or stagger flushes.

justin: plan: (1) reproduce with microbench (pairwise allreduce timing across msg sizes) (2) test NCCL_PROTO=LL128 + TREE as default for our TP config (3) add heuristic to bound per-step allreduce chunk to 128KB.

maya: I'll run pairwise microbench and upload numbers. if TREE + LL128 is consistently better for our topology, we should set that in kernel selection and add a runtime fallback to RING for tiny messages.

li: also add a perf counter for "KV flush bytes per step" so we can correlate spikes to cache behavior.

maya: ok I'll send a PR with microbench results and a patch to kernel selector to prefer TREE+LL128 for msg>=128KB, and RING+LL for msg<128KB. WIP.

maya: cc @omar @justin

omar: :thumbsup: keep the microbench small and reproducible. include scripts to run on both NVLink and PCIe nodes.

justin: if PR lands we'll canageroll on dedicated pool and monitor tail-latency.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled to dedicated-dev cluster after PR merge. :robot_face:

maya: thanks — will update thread with numbers and PR link.
